subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Adapted and Lifelong Inclusive Activity Design
essentialQuestion: How does an activity have to change to still be there at forty, or after an injury?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of activity across a lifespan and how demands change in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe adapting an activity after injury, illness, or changed capability using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving designing activity for a group with mixed ages and abilities; correct it and explain why.
Connect the social side: finding people to be active with as an adult with letting go of an activity without letting go of activity and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Take one activity the learner values and produce three adapted versions of it — for reduced mobility, for very limited time, and for a mixed-age group — with the reasoning for each.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Adaptations may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically; practical trial is optional.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
